source.title: NerveBeam LED Light Therapy Wrap - Paintechnology.com
source.heading: NerveBeam LED Light Therapy Wrap
source.content:
PRODUCTS
 Light Therapy 
 NerveBeam LED Light Therapy Wrap

 Roll over to zoom in

 + View large image

 NerveBeam LED Light Therapy Wrap

Clinical Device

Red & Infrared Light Therapy for Pain Relief, Circulation, Tissue Warming, and Muscle Relaxation

 Relieve Pain Designed to relieve minor muscle, joint, and nerve-related pain with red and infrared light therapy.
 Improve Circulation Temporarily increases local blood circulation in targeted treatment areas.
 Elevate Tissue Temperature Delivers heat-oriented light therapy support to warm tissues and promote comfort.
 Relax Muscles & Relieve Stiffness Promotes muscle relaxation, helps reduce tension, and supports range of motion.
 Support Healing Works on a cellular level to support the body’s natural healing processes more efficiently.

 PRODUCT CODE: NBRT175

 THERAPY INFO

 WARRANTY

 DESCRIPTION

Clinical Overview

High-Powered Red and Infrared Light Therapy Designed for Broad-Surface Clinical Use

The NerveBeam LED Light Therapy Wrap is a high-powered red light and infrared light therapy device designed to elevate tissue temperature, temporarily relieve minor muscle and joint pain, and temporarily improve local blood circulation across a broad treatment area.

Red light at 660 nm is positioned for surface-level tissue exposure, while infrared light at 830 nm and 850 nm are intended for surface and deeper thermal support. With flexible straps, broad treatment coverage, and high LED density, the NerveBeam is designed for freeform placement across multiple body regions in both clinic and provider-guided home-use workflows.

Clinical Applications

Versatile for Pain Relief, Circulation Support, Tissue Warming, and Mobility-Oriented Care

 Muscle and joint discomfort – temporary relief for minor muscle and joint pain.
 Circulation support – helps temporarily increase local blood circulation.
 Stiff or tense tissue – heat-oriented support for muscle relaxation and stiffness reduction.
 Nerve discomfort and recovery routines – adjunctive support in broader mobility and recovery workflows.
 Clinic-to-home continuity – broad-surface light therapy for provider-guided follow-through outside the clinic.

Key Focus Areas: Pain relief • Circulation support • Tissue warming • Muscle relaxation • Stiffness reduction

Light Therapy Features

Broad-Surface Coverage with High LED Density and Flexible Placement

 Red & Infrared Light Therapy – combines visible red light at 660 nm with infrared light at 830 nm and 850 nm.
 High-Density LED Power – 600 individual LED diodes with 22,000 mW total output for broad treatment coverage.
 Heat Therapy & Tissue Warming – reaches temperatures over 100 degrees Fahrenheit to help elevate tissue temperature and promote comfort.
 Freeform Body Placement – adjustable straps support flexible placement across upper- and lower-body treatment areas.
 Broad Treatment Area – designed to treat more surface area than narrow point-contact devices.
 Provider-Guided Continuity – appropriate for clinic use and provider-guided home routines.

Clinical Pathways

Designed for Flexible Use Across Pain, Recovery, and Mobility-Oriented Workflows

Pain Relief Support

The NerveBeam may be applied over joints, muscle groups, and other targeted regions to help temporarily relieve minor muscle and joint pain while supporting comfort during broader care plans.

Circulation & Tissue Warming

 DESCRIPTION

Nerve Target Roll-On Gel: Science-Led Topical Sensory & Microvascular Support

Localized musculoskeletal discomfort is commonly associated with transient inflammatory mediator signaling, altered peripheral sensory receptor activation, and microvascular circulation shifts.

Nerve Target Roll-On Gel is a clinician-developed topical formulation designed to support sensory receptor modulation and localized circulation using counterirritant compounds and botanical extracts evaluated in controlled human research.*

Formulation Strategy: Convergent Sensory & Circulatory Support

This formulation integrates TRP-channel activators, vasomodulatory botanicals, and antioxidant-rich plant extracts studied for their roles in sensory signaling and localized comfort.

TRP Channel Sensory Modulation

Menthol

Menthol activates TRPM8 receptors and has been evaluated in controlled human trials for topical cooling-mediated analgesic effects.

Camphor

Camphor has been studied for topical counterirritant effects and modulation of peripheral sensory receptors.

Microcirculatory Support

Eucalyptus (Eucalyptus globulus leaf)

Eucalyptus oil has been evaluated in human trials examining anti-inflammatory and topical comfort endpoints.

Arnica

Studied in randomized controlled trials evaluating musculoskeletal comfort.

Botanical Antioxidant Support

Camellia sinensis (Green Tea Leaf)

Evaluated in human research for antioxidant and inflammatory biomarker modulation.

Dosing & Application

Apply to affected area up to 3–4 times daily.
For external use only.

Designed for localized use as part of a comprehensive musculoskeletal support strategy.

Formulation Standards

 Third-party laboratory tested
 No artificial dyes
 Manufactured in the USA in GMP-compliant facilities

Selected Clinical Research Context

The ingredient components within this formulation have been evaluated in controlled human trials examining sensory receptor activation, topical analgesic endpoints, inflammatory biomarker modulation, and musculoskeletal function outcomes.

Menthol (TRPM8 activation)

Galeotti et al., Pain (2002)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12406524/

Camphor

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17318618/

Eucalyptus Oil (Topical)

Jun et al., Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine (2013))
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23662106/

 DESCRIPTION

The Nerve Spa Knee is based off of a clinically proven, non-invasive, non-drug treatment option for osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee. The Nerve Spa Knee system delivers a proprietary electrical signal that stimulates the joint tissue to reduce the pain and symptoms of Osteoarthritis and Rheumatoid Arthritis, and helps maintain the overall health of the knee joint.

The Nerve Spa Knee is a hybrid development using the technical specifications of the Nerve Spa combined with the technical specifications of the Jstim Joint stimulator.  The Jstim device is backed by over 15 years of positive results in treating the joint.

Nerve Spa Knee’s advanced signal was designed specifically for the treatment of pain and symptoms of knee OA and RA, however, the device can be used for other knee pain ailments and to ultimately prevent the deterioration of the knee joint by active individuals.

The Nerve Spa stimulates the joint, the tissue, the tendons, ligaments and the cartilage. Our proprietary hybrid-programming works to regenerate cartilage and improve the overall health of the joint. It is a slow-acting, aggregate therapy, to help progressively improve the knee’s function.

The Nerve Spa Joint Pro is built with comfort and convenience in mind:

The Joint Pro works by sending tiny electrical signals to the joint over a 1 hour therapy session to help relieve pain, increase blood circulation, and therapeutically treat the symptoms associated with OA and RA.

Stimulation should be adjusted to a very mild sensory level.

KNEE SPRAIN

A sprain is an injury to a ligament, the bands of tissue that connect a bone to another at a joint. The severity of a sprain can be characterized by the amount of tissue tearing, impact on joint stability, pain and/or swelling.

LIGAMENT INJURY

The knee joint relies on ligaments (ACL, PCL, MCL, LCL) and surrounding muscles for stability, so they can be easily injured. Any direct contact to the knee or rapid direction changes while moving can injure a knee ligament.

RUNNERS’ KNEE

Runners’ knee, also known as patellofemoral pain syndrome, is described as pain located beneath or around the kneecap. Running can cause irritation where the kneecap rests on the thigh bone (femur) and the pain is aggravated by bending at the knees and using stairs. Stiffness in the knee after prolonged sitting is also a symptom of runners knee.

OSTEOARTHRITIS

Osteoarthritis, also known as degenerative joint disease, is the most common type of arthritis. Osteoarthritis is more likely to develop as people age and have increased weight on the joint. The onset of osteoarthritis usually occurs slowly over many years. Inflammation and injury to the joint cause a breaking down of cartilage tissues, resulting in pain, swelling, and deformity of the joint.

The targeted Joint Stimulation is cumulative and combinational to provide clear and apparent progressive results.

The following is a summary of an independent study completed for Technology contained within the Joint Pro device

Five women ranging in age from 51 to 68 with radiologically diagnosed OA of the knee, suffering chronic pain which limited their activity level and in some cases interfered with sleep, received home treatment for 10 weeks. Three indicators were compared before and after treatment: (1) qualitapatients reported that their knee pain and function showed substantial; (2) a 44-point subjective quantitative Lower Extremity Functional Scale was customized for this population, and improvement for the group averaged 33% (9.4 was measured by a physician, and increase for the group averaged 19% (11 degrees) with 4 of 5 patients improving. Three of the 5 patients showed improvement in all 3 indicators, and among the 15 individual indicators positive change occurred in 87% (13 of 15). In this trial the Jstim demonstrated excellent potential for reducing pain and dysfunction caused by osteoarthritis in the knee.
_the study was conducted by Stuart Greenleaf, L.Ac. and Dr. Jerry Evans

 DESCRIPTION

The NerveSpa Classic is an Advanced Nerve and Neuropathy stimulator that utilizes a hybrid of electrotherapy specifications drawing from enhanced Micro-Current, and Galvanic stim, combined with proprietary programming to specifically target the nerve to therapeutically treat early-onset and mid-stage peripheral neuropathy, as well other nerve-based pain conditions in the hands and feet.

Benefits of the Nerve Spa Nerve Stim

 The Nerve Spa provides a hybrid wave form to assist in repairing, rebuilding, and staving off nerve degeneration.
 The Nerve spa conducts the current through one foot, up the leg, to the low back, and down the other leg, and to the other foot. This helps reestablish nerve pathways

NerveSpa Program stands apart from other nerve therapy devices through advanced programming, deep research, and a guided protocol—for comprehensive, full-foot and hand, nerve engagement.

The Nerve Spa harnesses a sweepable 7.83Hz Frequency, however with a unique spiked monophasic pulsed waveform that is notably effective at pushing fluids and treating conditions in one's extremities - hands and feet. The Nerve Spa also utilizes a microprocessor to modulate the waveform to asymmetrical biphasic pulse and other settings to dispel negative ion charge build-up in the tissue. The Nerve Spa works by mimicking the signals of a healthy nerve and revitalizing damaged or dying nerves, through targeted electrical pulses.

Unlike traditional devices that rely solely on surface electrode pads, NerveSpa’s stimulation delivers even and effective coverage to the entire foot, while ensuring maximum comfort and efficacy of the tech specs reaching all parts of the afflicted appendage.

Engineered for Results:

 Full-Foot Stimulation: Delivers consistent, therapeutic stimulation across all nerve zones—unlike pad-based competitors that treat only limited surface areas.
 High-Volt Currency: Unlike traditional TENS or other nerve stimulators, the Nerve Spa is a high volt, high amplitude stimulation coupled with a low level frequency.
 Advanced Programming Experience: The Nervespa team harnesses a deep knowledge base and understanding of the foundational principles of electrotherapy, and the next frontier innovations around technical parameters in treating conditions.  Commitment to Innovation: The Nerve Spa has evolved through over 15 different software and programming updates to balance out the complexities of stimulating the nerves through an aquatic stimulation process, as well as further the sensory level, and efficacy in treating the nerve in the most capable way possible to increase the likelihood of Neuropathic results.

For a detailed feature-by-feature comparison—including comfort, hygiene, setup, and clinical application—please refer to our comparison chart comparison chart or contact our team for a personalized demo..

Are your feet burning
and tingling?

The peripheral nervous system connects the nerves running from the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body including the arms and hands, legs and feet.

Nerve damage in the feet occurs when nerves are injured or destroyed and can't send messages from the brain to your extremities and vice versa.

When damage occurs, numbness and pain in these areas may occur, and often can be excruciating.

The NerveSpa family of products are all specially designed to calm the nerves and treat the affected areas which allows the nerve cells the potential to recover.

If you're suffering from nerve damage in your feet, nerve pain or painful numbness, then we invite you to learn more about how NerveSpa can deliver safe and effective results.

 60-90-Day, Drug-Free Treatment to Reduce Pain

Aquatic Electrotherapy Stimulation

 7.83Hz Symmetrical Biphasic Square & Monophasic Waveform

 The Symmetrical Biphasic wave helps quell pain, while the Monophasic waveform pushes fluids and enhances pain relief in one's extremities.

 Rechargeable Battery

 Touch Screen Device with Proprietary Output Parameters

 Control intensity level with a simple to use touch screen.An auto-play plrogram makes it easy-to-use.

Use As Part of the NerveSpa 90-Day Program

source.question: How long do TENS pads last?
source.answer: TENS electrodes typically last 10-30 uses,depending on the quality of the pads, how often they are used, skin condition, and how well they are cared for. Replace pads when they lose stickiness or stimulation becomes uneven.

source.question: Is a TENS unit safe to use during pregnancy?
source.answer: TENS may be used during pregnancy in some cases, but it is best to consult with your healthcare provider before use. Many providers recommend avoiding certain areas, especially the abdomen, lower back, pelvis, and acupuncture points that may stimulate contractions. When approved by a healthcare professional, TENS is sometimes used during pregnancy for issues such as back discomfort or labor related pain.

tests.question: Where is the right place to put the pads for neck pain?

source.question: Where do I put the pads for neck pain?
source.answer: For neck pain, place the TENS pads on the muscles along the sides and back of the neck, near the area of discomfort. Avoid placing pads directly on the front or sides of the throat, the head, or over the spine. Common placements include: one pad on each side of the neck muscles, or putting the pads above and below the painful area along the upper shoulders and neck.

tests.question: What steps should I follow to know which pads are best for me?

source.question: How do I know which pads are best for me?
source.answer: The best TENS pads depend on where you are treating, the size of the area, and your comfort preference. Consider: Small pads: Best for targeted areas like wrists, ankles, elbows, or smaller joints. Large pads: Best for larger areas like the lower back, shoulders, hips or thighs. Longer Lasting Pads: Better for frequent users who need more repeated sessions. Flexible Pads: Helpful for areas that move often, like knees, shoulders, or joints. For the best results, choose pads that provide good skin contact,comfortable stimulation, and proper coverage for your treatment area.

tests.question: What could cause my TENS unit turn on not to work?

source.question: Why won't my TENS unit turn on?
source.answer: If your TENS unit will not power on, the issue is usually related to the battery, charging, or a connection problem. Try these steps: Check the battery: Replace disposable batteries or fully charge the device if it is rechargable. Confirm proper battery placement: Make sure batteries are inserted correctly and making contact. Try a different charger or cable: If rechargable, check that the charging cable and power source are working. Hold the power button: Some units require pressing and holding the button for a few seconds. Check for damage: Look for cracks, loose parts, or signs of moisture exposure. Disconnect accessories: Remove lead wires and pads, then try turning the unit on again. Review the user manual: Some devices have specific startup steps or safety locks.

tests.question: Is it okay for me to use a TENS unit if I have metal implants?

source.question: Can I use a TENS unit if I have metal implants?
source.answer: In many cases, yes, TENS can be used with metal implants, such as joint replacements or surgical hardware. The electrical stimulation from a TENS unit typically does not affect non-electronic metal implants. However, you should check with your healthcare provider before use, especially if the implant is near the treatment area or if you have any type of electronic implant (such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, or nerve stimulator).

tests.question: What steps should I follow to make my pads sticky again?

source.question: How do I make my pads sticky again?
source.answer: TENS pads cannot usually be made fully sticky again, as once the conductive gel has dried out, it is not recommended to try and make them sticky again. This can cause burns or rash due to the gel drying out. Once pads have started to lose their adhesive, it is recommended to swap out with new electrodes for proper use and safety purposes.

source.question: How do I read the battery level indicator on my Ultima 5?
source.answer: The battery icon on your display uses a simple 2-bar system. Both bars showing means your battery is fully charged. One bar means you're at a mid-level charge. source.question: What frequency works best for acute pain?
source.answer: For acute pain (new or short-term pain from an injury, procedure, or strain), many users find higher frequencies around 50-120 Hz helpful. These settings may provide faster relief by helping interrupt pain signals traveling to the brain. Lower frequencies may also be used depending on the type of pain and individual response.

tests.question: Could you explain this for me: What settings should I use for my very first Ultima 5 session?

source.question: What settings should I use for my very first Ultima 5 session?
source.answer: Your Quick Start Guide recommends a simple starting point: set the frequency to 150Hz, the pulse width to 250us, and the mode to Constant. Turn the intensity up to a level that feels strong but comfortable, and use the unit for 30-45 minutes, or as long as needed. For your wave form, start with the Asymmetrical Bi-Phasic Rectangular setting, it's the recommended starting point for initial treatment. From there, feel free to adjust based on comfort and results.

tests.question: In practical terms, I need to understand this: What are the theories behind how TENS units work.

source.question: What are the theories behind how TENS units work?
source.answer: There are two leading theories that explain why TENS provides relief, and understanding them can help you get more out of your device. The first is the Gate Control Theory of Pain. It suggests that the electrical pulses from your TENS unit travel along nerve fibers faster than pain signals do, effectively closing a "gate" in your spinal cord so fewer pain signals reach your brain. This is generally associated with higher frequency settings and tends to provide faster, more immediate relief. The second is the Endorphin Release Theory, which suggests that certain settings, typically lower frequencies, encourage your body to release endorphins, its own natural pain-relieving chemicals. This effect tends to build more gradually and can last longer after your session ends. Many people find that combining both approaches, or simply experimenting with frequency over a few sessions, helps them find what works best for their body.

tests.question: Could you give me the important information behind this question: Can I wear a TENS unit all day?

source.question: Can I wear a TENS unit all day?
source.answer: It is generally not recommended to wear a TENS unit continuously all day without breaks. While TENS can often be used multiple times throughout the day, extended use may increase the risk of skin irritation, reduced effectiveness, or discomfort. For best results: Use TENS in scheduled sessions as needed. Give your skin breaks between treatments. Move electrode placement if using the same area frequently. Follow your device's recommended usage guidelines.

source.question: Are generic pads compatible with my unit?
source.answer: In most cases, yes, generic TENS pads are compatible as long as they use the same standard pin size for connection and are designed for TENS/EMS devices. Before purchasing, check the following: The connector type (most use a standard 2mm pin or snap connection). The pad size and shape are the correct size for your treatment area. The manufacturer's recommendations for your specific device. Higher-quality electrodes often provide better adhesion, comfort, and consistent stimulation compared to lower-quality alternatives.

source.question: Why does my skin turn red after treatment?
source.answer: Mild redness after using a TENS unit can be normal and is often caused by increased circulation, pressure from the electrode, or mild skin sensitivity. It should typically fade shortly after removing the pads. To reduce skin irritation: Make sure your skin is clean and dry before use. Avoid placing pads on irritated or damaged skin. Rotate pad placement between treatments. Reduce treatment intensity if the sensation feels uncomfortable. Replace electrodes when the gel becomes old or irritating.

source.question: Can I place the pads directly over where the pain is?
source.answer: Yes. Tens PADS can often be placed near or around the area of pain to help target discomfort. However, avoid placing pads directly over the areas where they are not recommended, such as the front of the neck, head, open wounds, irritated skin, or directly over bony areas. For the best results, try placing the pads around the painful area rather than directly on the most sensitive spot.

tests.question: why won't my pads stick anmyore

source.question: Why won't my pads stick anymore?
source.answer: TENS pads can lose their stickiness over time due to repeated use, moisture, oils, lotions, dirt, or improper storage. As the gel dries out or the pads are used, the pads may not make proper contact with the skin, which will reduce stimulation quality. Once you are noticing that your pads are sticking less, or are starting to fall off the skin, it is recommended to swap out your pads for new. To improve pad life: Clean and dry your skin before applying pads. Avoid using lotions, oils, or creams before treatment. Store pads on their backing sheet in a sealed bag or container. Replace pads when the gel becomes dry, dirty, or no longer adheres well.

source.question: What is the Lock/Unlock feature, and how do I use it?
source.answer: The Lock/Unlock feature lets you hold your current intensity steady so it can't be accidentally bumped up or down mid-session, handy if the unit is clipped to your belt or moving around while you're active. tests.question: Why does my unit keep turning off Also, how should I approach electrode placement?

source.question: Why does my unit keep turning off?
source.answer: If your TENS unit keeps shutting off, it is usually caused by a power, connection, or safety feature issue. Common issues include: Low battery: Replace or recharge the batteries to ensure the unit has enough power. Automatic Shutoff Timer: Many TENS units turn off automatically after a set treatment time. Loose connections: Check that the lead wires are fully connected to the unit and electrode pads. Poor pad contact: If the pads lose contact with the skin, some units may pause or stop stimulation. Damaged cables or electrodes: Worn pads or faulty wires can interrupt the connection. Intensity set too high: Some devices may stop if they detect an issue with the electrical connection.

answer: If your TENS unit keeps shutting off, it is usually caused by a power, connection, or safety feature issue. Common issues include: Low battery: Replace or recharge the batteries to ensure the unit has enough power. Automatic Shutoff Timer: Many TENS units turn off automatically after a set treatment time. Loose connections: Check that the lead wires are fully connected to the unit and electrode pads. Poor pad contact: If the pads lose contact with the skin, some units may pause or stop stimulation. Damaged cables or electrodes: Worn pads or faulty wires can interrupt the connection. Intensity set too high: Some devices may stop if they detect an issue with the electrical connection.

Proper electrode placement can make a big difference in how comfortable and effective your TENS treatment feels. The goal is to place pads where they can best influence the area of discomfort. Helpful Guidelines: Place pads around the painful area: Position electrodes on either side of the pain or along the surrounding muscles. Avoid placing pads directly over irritated or damaged skin. Keep pads evenly spaced: Proper spacing helps create a consistent stimulation pathway. Use both channels when available: This allows you to treat larger areas or multiple areas at the same time. Adjust placement if needed: Small changes in the pad location can improve comfort and sensation. Follow your device's instructions: Some conditions may have recommended placement patterns.

source.question: What does a TENS unit feel like?
source.answer: Most users describe the sensation as: a gentle tingling, a light buzzing, mild tapping or pulsing, or a comfortable vibration. The intensity should be strong, but comfortable. A TENS unit should never be painful. If you experience sharp, burning, or uncomfortable sensations, reduce the intensity or check that the electrode pads are properly positioned and making good contact with your skin.
answerAlternatives:
Most users describe the sensation as: a gentle tingling, a light buzzing, mild tapping or pulsing, or a comfortable vibration. The intensity should be strong, but comfortable. A TENS unit should never be painful. source.question: Can I drive while using a TENS unit?
source.answer: It is not recommended to drive or operate heavy machinery while using a TENS unit. The stimulation can be distracting, and changes in intensity or muscle responses may affect your ability to drive safely. For your safety, use your TENS unit before or after driving rather than while operating a vehicle.

The stimulation can be distracting, and changes in intensity or muscle responses may affect your ability to drive safely. For your safety, use your TENS unit before or after driving rather than while operating a vehicle.

Once you make your first adjustment to pulse rate or pulse width, an auto-repeat function kicks in. If you press and hold the "PR+", "PR-", "PW+", or "PW-" key for about 1 second, the value will keep increasing or decreasing automatically, one step every quarter-second, so you can dial in your setting faster without repeatedly tapping the button.

source.question: What are typical troubleshooting issues with TENS units?
source.answer: Most issues come down to power, connections, pad contact, or settings. No sensation? Check the lead wires are seated and pads are on clean skin with intensity turned up. Weak or uneven feel? Replace worn electrodes. Unexpected shutoff? Usually the timer, low battery, or a safety response to poor contact. Your Ultima 5's Pad Contact Alarm flashes "CH1"/"CH2" if a connection starts failing.

 External vacuum erection devices have become easily available for consumers since the FDA no longer requires a prescription from a physician to purchase a penis pump. Originally the device required a prescription when introduced in 1982. Prescription requirements were removed in 1997 when the FDA determined the medical penis pump as safe and highly effective.
 Although prescriptions are no longer required, safety and quality issues are addressed by FDA guidelines and enforced by FDA inspectors. A medical device is held to high manufacturing standards. Pumps that are not medical grade may not work properly. They may also pose health risks to users of these products.

 PRODUCT CODE: PMT-ECVED

 THERAPY INFO

 WARRANTY

 Manual

 Premium

 DESCRIPTION

Guide to Penis Pumps: Benefits and Types

Using a medical penis pump has several benefits, and acquiring one has become more accessible to consumers since the FDA's prescription requirement was lifted in 1997. These devices are held to high manufacturing standards, ensuring both safety and effectiveness. Here are some advantages of using a medical device penis pump:

 Non-Invasive Treatment: Unlike other treatments for erectile dysfunction (ED), such as oral medications, injections, or surgical implants, penis pumps offer a non-invasive option with fewer adverse health risks.
 Compatibility with Medical Conditions: Some men may find oral medications unsuitable due to underlying health conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes. A penis pump can be a safe and effective alternative for these individuals.
 Cost-Effective: Compared to surgical implants or shockwave therapy, which can be costly and may not have proven effectiveness, medical-grade penis pumps offer a more affordable option for ED treatment.
 Penile Rehabilitation: Following procedures like prostate cancer treatment, penile rehabilitation with a penis pump can help prevent issues like penile shrinkage and tissue atrophy.
 Complementary Treatment: Penis pumps can be used in conjunction with other ED treatments to enhance their effectiveness, providing a fuller and more sustained erection.

Types of Penis Pumps:

 Water Penis Pump: Utilizing water instead of air, these pumps are designed for use in water, typically in the bathtub or shower. They're not commonly used for sexual intercourse.
 Manual Penis Pump: The most common type, operated manually with a pumping device connected to the cylinder.
 Electric Penis Pump: These devices are powered electrically and are beneficial for individuals with conditions like arthritis or those who prefer automated operation.

Choosing the Right Device:

When selecting a penis pump, ensure it's FDA-registered and meets quality standards. Consider factors like cylinder size options and tension systems for maintaining erections comfortably. Beware of misleading claims by some products regarding penis enlargement, as no device is cleared by the FDA for such purposes.

Using a Penis Pump:

Proper preparation is essential for optimal results with a penis pump. This includes familiarizing yourself with the device, trimming pubic hair, applying lubricant, and experimenting with tension systems to find the best fit.

Insurance Coverage:

While most insurance providers no longer cover external penis pumps, they remain one of the most cost-effective forms of ED treatment compared to other options like medications or implants.

source.content:
PRODUCTS
 Massage Therapy Devices 
 Shoulder Rotator Cuff Stretching Device By Stretch Towel; Physical Therapy Shoulder And Full Body Stretching Strap With Easy Grip Handles for Sore and Tight Muscles. Improves Shoulder Flexibility

 Roll over to zoom in

 + View large image

 Shoulder Rotator Cuff Stretching Device By Stretch Towel; Physical Therapy Shoulder And Full Body Stretching Strap With Easy Grip Handles for Sore and Tight Muscles. Improves Shoulder Flexibility

 PERFECT SHOULDER STRETCH – The Stretch Towel is designed to perform a targeted stretch on the rotator cuff to help improve shoulder flexibility

 FULL BODY STRETCHING – Use the Stretch Towel to perform a variety of other body part stretches

 VERSITILE – One-Size-Fits All, Easily adjustable to fit all body types

 MACHINE WASHABLE – Machine washable, and air dry for best use.

 PRODUCT CODE: STROT10

 THERAPY INFO

 WARRANTY

 DESCRIPTION
 The Stretch Towel is an essential tool in helping to stretch the rotator cuff as well as other body parts. To effectively use the Stretch Towel for shoulder exercises it is essential to use it correctly or you won’t gain the right result. The towel is securely wrapped around the shoulder, as the user pushes their arm forward, the towel engages around the shoulder and creates a counter lever, and tightening effect that creates a tension that drives the stretch.  Very few products on the market can provide an effective stretch to the rotator cuff, and the Stretch Towel Delivers.
 Summary of User Steps
1. Hang or drape the Stretch Towel over your neck with one side hanging lower than the other.
2. Next you will take the longer end, and wrap it back around the shoulder while grabbing the handle of that same side 
3. Once you have it wrapped around the shoulder and all is in position, you can perform the stretch. 
4. Pull downward on the handle of the opposing arm to provide tension. Then on the arm that the towel is wrapped around, while the handle and grip is in the horizontal position, begin to rotate the forearm downward/forward as if you are sweeping a 45 degree angle motion. 
5. You should feel the towel grab and pull on the shoulder, thus stretching the shoulder in this process. 
6. Perform this stretch 15 times while holding it in position to form a greater stretch.

 SPECIFICATIONS

 Product Weight (lbs) : 1

tests.question: How would you describe what a TENS unit feels like?

source.question: What does a TENS unit feel like?
source.answer: Most users describe the sensation as: a gentle tingling, a light buzzing, mild tapping or pulsing, or a comfortable vibration. The intensity should be strong, but comfortable. A TENS unit should never be painful. If you experience sharp, burning, or uncomfortable sensations, reduce the intensity or check that the electrode pads are properly positioned and making good contact with your skin.

PRODUCTS

 NERVE & NEUROPATHY CREAM - Topical Microvascular & Sensory Support Formula

 Roll over to zoom in

 NERVE & NEUROPATHY CREAM - Topical Microvascular & Sensory Support Formula

 SUPPORTS TARGETED COMFORT
(Menthol + Arnica + MSM)

 SUPPORTS HEALTHY MICRO-CIRCULATION
(L-Arginine 7 g + Vitamin B6)

 PROMOTES FAST LOCAL ABSORPTION
(Plant Oils + Lipid Carriers)

 SOOTHES & CALMS PERIPHERAL TISSUE
(Aloe + Allantoin + Botanical Extracts)

 PRODUCT CODE: NNC10

 THERAPY INFO

 WARRANTY

 DESCRIPTION

Nerve & Neuropathy Cream: Science-Led Topical Support for Peripheral Microcirculation & Sensory Comfort

Peripheral sensory discomfort is frequently associated with altered microvascular perfusion, inflammatory mediator signaling, and localized tissue stress. Clinicians supporting peripheral nerve discomfort commonly observe impaired nitric oxide signaling, oxidative imbalance, and reduced endothelial responsiveness at the local tissue level.

Nerve & Neuropathy Cream is a clinician-developed topical formulation designed for localized application to reinforce microvascular pathways, nitric oxide signaling, and tissue-calming mechanisms using clinically studied ingredients.

Formulation Strategy: Convergent Microvascular & Sensory Support

The formulation integrates nitric oxide precursors, topical counterirritants, antioxidant cofactors, and tissue-calming botanicals to support localized vascular and sensory physiology identified in controlled human research.

Nitric Oxide & Local Circulation Support

L-Arginine (7 g, 8.4%)supports nitric oxide production and endothelial responsiveness. Topical and systemic nitric oxide pathways have been studied in microvascular perfusion research.

Counterirritant & Sensory Modulation

Menthol (2,000 mg) activates TRPM8 receptors and has been evaluated in controlled studies for topical analgesic effects and cooling-mediated sensory modulation.

Botanical Microvascular Modulators

Arnica has been studied in controlled trials examining topical application and musculoskeletal discomfort endpoints.

MSM (Methylsulfonylmethane) has been evaluated in randomized controlled trials examining inflammatory and musculoskeletal parameters.

Vitamin Cofactor Support

Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine HCl) supports enzymatic processes involved in neurotransmitter synthesis and peripheral nerve metabolism.

Antioxidant & Tissue-Soothing Support

Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Powder has been evaluated in dermatologic research for topical soothing and wound-support applications.

Tocopheryl Acetate (Vitamin E) supports lipid membrane stability and antioxidant balance in topical applications.

Dosing & Application

Apply to affected area up to 3–4 times daily.
For external use only.

Designed for localized use as part of a comprehensive peripheral support strategy.

Formulation Standards

Third-party laboratory tested
No artificial dyes or synthetic additives
Manufactured in the USA in GMP-compliant facilities

Selected Clinical Research Context

The ingredient components within this formulation have been evaluated in controlled human trials examining vascular, sensory, and inflammatory-related endpoints.

L-Arginine

Evaluated in randomized trials assessing nitric oxide bioavailability and
endothelial-dependent vasodilation.
Böger RH. Circulation (1998)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9456007/

Menthol

Studied in controlled trials examining topical cooling and sensory modulation
mechanisms.
Galeotti et al., Pain (2002)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12406524/

Arnica

Evaluated in randomized controlled trials examining topical musculoskeletal discomfort endpoints.
Widrig et al., Rheumatology International (2007)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17318618/

MSM

Examined in randomized trials evaluating inflammatory and joint-related parameters.
Kim et al., Osteoarthritis Cartilage (2006)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16309928/

These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.
